proposed_from.topic: Sharp single-bin facet envelope for arbitrary finite coarsened-exposure IV bounds. Observe iid (Z,X,Y) with randomized binary Z, binary Y, finite X={a,b,c_1,...,c_m}, and a declared trusted set T containing a,b whose category interventions are well defined and satisfy exclusion and consistency; untrusted categories impose no cross-Z outcome restriction. For theta_ab=E[Y(b)-Y(a)], prove the identified interval is sharp and its lower/upper endpoints are the eight binary-exposure Balke-Pearl affine pieces plus exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category. Derive a complete two-diagonal transport reduction, explicit endpoint-attaining finite response laws, the exact strict-improvement criterion for adding trust, and invariance to splitting or merging wholly untrusted bins. Give an O(|X|) endpoint/active-face evaluator and finite-sample simultaneous whole-set inference valid at ties and zero cells. Consumer: Du Toit et al.'s LEAP adherence analysis, where the theorem determines whether separately justified intermediate exposure categories can change the assumption-free low-versus-high consumption interval. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Coupling the two instrument-arm factual responses on a complete bipartite graph minus a partial matching reduces the lower endpoint to maximizing mass on two target diagonals. After reserving those masses, feasibility has two individual caps and one total cap per trusted nuisance outcome cell; exact maximization yields the claimed affine envelope, and a finite augmenting-path completion constructs attaining laws. Checks passed 840 response-LP cases for 2-8 exposure categories and all trust cardinalities, 32 saturated-response cases, and 9,648 exact rational endpoint constructions; maximum LP discrepancy was 7.78e-16. LEAP arm denominators 305 and 312 reproduce the low-minus-high interval [-5073/31720,10/61]. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently formalize and verify the transport domination and endpoint-completion argument; the optional moment-selected Gaussian multiplier procedure still needs a uniform local-tie/vanishing-variance proof, while finite-sample Hoeffding whole-set coverage is already derived. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate legal denominator-three four-category tables under every trust subset containing a,b and reconstruct both reserved-diagonal endpoint laws exactly; stop if any residual flow, margin, or objective equality fails. seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The Introduction, Results 1--4, the displayed ternary bounds in Section 2.3, the LEAP analysis, and the Discussion were read in the arXiv source. The Discussion explicitly asks whether the observed pattern extends to arbitrary exposure cardinality.
seed_details.question: For binary \(Z\) and \(Y\), arbitrary finite \(X\), and exclusion imposed only on a trusted subset containing \(a\) and \(b\), is the sharp interval for \(\theta_{ab}\) the eight Balke--Pearl pieces plus two affine pieces for each trusted nuisance category, with no mixed-nuisance pieces?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Song et al.'s coupling between one factual arm and a full vector of potential outcomes by a coupling of the two factual arm distributions whose forbidden relation is only a partial matching; then optimize two selected diagonal masses before completing the residual flow.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for mixed-validity categorical-IV bounds, partial-matching transport, arbitrary coarsened exposures, and citing work found Gabriel et al.'s ternary result and Song et al.'s full-validity characterization, but no arbitrary-cardinality selected-trust scalar envelope.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. because their Strassen inequalities already characterize every finite categorical IV model.
seed_details.rebuttal: Song et al. impose exclusion for every treatment category and leave the pairwise ATE as an optimization over a full counterfactual distribution; deleting exclusion category by category changes the coherence graph, and their theorem neither yields the \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) projection nor endpoint-attaining mixed-validity laws.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the coupling-native M10 representation rather than presenting generic response-type linear programming as the contribution; the named focal object is the two-diagonal capacity \(D_T(p)\).

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The LEAP table and Section 4 comparison were read. They show that the trusted third-level faces can tighten in principle but do not change the LEAP interval, without an observable if-and-only-if rule.
seed_details.question: Give necessary and sufficient observable strict inequalities for whether declaring one additional nuisance category trusted raises the lower endpoint, lowers the upper endpoint, or reduces interval width.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving the affine endpoint envelope, compare the two new category faces to the old active envelope and distinguish strict replacement from a tie.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for categorical-IV identification gain, value of exclusion restrictions, and instrument identification power found Zhang et al.'s binary-ATE gain decomposition, but no category-specific trust criterion for coarsened treatments.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Gabriel et al. because adding their two third-level terms can only tighten the interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: Weak monotonicity is immediate, but exact strictness is not: the result must identify when a new face strictly overtakes the old maximum or minimum, handle equality ties, and apply one category at a time for arbitrary support.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is an if-and-only-if active-face theorem, not the qualitative claim that stronger assumptions cannot widen an identified set.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The homocysteine analysis and Discussion were read. Three-bin and four-bin codings give the same numerical interval, but no structural refinement theorem is stated.
seed_details.question: Show that the sharp pairwise interval factors through armwise totals after every split or merge wholly inside the untrusted region, and exhibit why a refinement that changes the trusted intervention semantics need not be invariant.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Push a feasible factual-arm coupling forward through the aggregation map and lift it back by disintegrating only unrestricted rows and columns; the lift fails at the first trusted edge deletion crossed by the map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing refinement invariance with coarsened-exposure IV bounds found Marshall's coarsening-bias result and VanderWeele--Hernan's treatment-version semantics, but no sharp-set quotient theorem under a selected trust boundary.
seed_details.red_team: A tautology because untrusted categories do not occur in the target potential outcomes.
seed_details.rebuttal: They still occur in both observed arm margins and in the coupling feasibility problem; invariance requires a two-sided pushforward and lifting result, while crossing a trusted boundary changes the forbidden-edge relation and can alter the interval.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is about equality of projected sharp sets under a quotient map, not merely equality of a displayed formula after relabeling.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Results 1 and 3 were read as the two endpoints of an all-or-nothing trust regime: exact exclusion adds faces, whereas direct instrument effects at the nuisance level collapse those gains.
seed_details.question: Replace hard trust by category-specific caps on direct instrument effects and derive a sharp piecewise-affine sensitivity path and the smallest violation radius at which a sign conclusion fails.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace deletion of a forbidden matching edge by a capacity on discrepant trusted-outcome flow and solve the resulting parametric transport dual across all breakpoints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing categorical IV, exclusion sensitivity, direct-effect caps, and response-function bounds found Conley et al.'s linear plausibly-exogenous model and Duarte et al.'s generic numerical programs, but no closed-form category-specific path.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic parametric linear programming because every sensitivity radius enters a right-hand side.
seed_details.rebuttal: A numerical parametric program does not identify the complete breakpoint set, prove a closed-form envelope, or construct attaining laws uniformly in the radii; those are the substantive open steps.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a critical violation radius and a sharp path, so it is not sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Sections 1.2, 6, and 8 of version 6 were read. The paper obtains simultaneous finite-sample coverage from one multinomial Kullback--Leibler region and explicitly leaves less-conservative confidence intervals for future work.
seed_details.question: Construct simultaneous Gaussian-multiplier endpoint inference that is uniformly valid under local face ties and vanishing face variances, with a boundary-safe fallback and a strict first-order width gain on regular interiors.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Estimate the directional derivative of the finite max/min map on a near-active face set, then prove anti-concentration and selection validity without dividing by a variance that may vanish.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multiplier inference at affine-face ties and vanishing variance located Fang--Santos directional bootstrap and Chernozhukov--Lee--Rosen moment selection, but not their uniform combination at multinomial boundary cells.
seed_details.red_team: A finite envelope is a textbook directionally differentiable functional, so Fang and Santos already solve the problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their general derivative bootstrap does not by itself establish uniform validity for simultaneous sequences with zero multinomial cells and collapsing face variances, nor the proposed regular-interior precision comparison.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is a limit-law and uniformity frontier, labeled M11(c), rather than a bare inference modifier.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Theorem 1 and the sufficiency proof were read. Their armwise Strassen couplings are glued through a common full potential-outcome margin for arbitrary finite \(Z\).
seed_details.question: For finite multi-arm \(Z\) and binary \(Y\), characterize pairwise ATE bounds when exclusion holds only on a selected treatment subset, and determine whether a polynomial-size transport representation survives.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The two-arm direct coupling becomes a multi-marginal compatibility problem; the first unresolved move is whether the partial matching restrictions admit a common latent response law without exponentially many mixed-arm constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multi-arm instruments with category-specific treatment exclusion found Song et al.'s global exclusion model and Gabriel et al.'s three-arm small-support calculations, but no arbitrary mixed-trust theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying Song et al.'s theorem to each arm after deleting untrusted coordinates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deleting coordinates removes the common consistency relation but does not remove their observed masses; pairwise arm couplings need not glue to one response law, so an additional multi-marginal step is required.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed identifies the failed gluing step rather than claiming a routine binary-to-multilevel extension.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and the nonredundancy count were read. For nonbinary \(Y\), non-singleton coordinate subsets generate additional necessary faces even under full trust.
seed_details.question: For ordered finite outcomes, find a computable sharp pairwise mean-effect support function under selected trust and determine whether the binary two-diagonal reduction becomes a bounded collection of outcome-level transports.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The edgewise minimum effect is no longer determined by membership in two binary diagonals; it becomes a min-cost transport problem with several outcome-cost levels and potentially mixed trusted-category cuts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining nonbinary outcomes, categorical treatment, mixed exclusion, and sharp IV support functions found Song et al.'s full-trust polytope but no selected-trust closed form.
seed_details.red_team: Song et al.'s finite linear program already computes every linear mean contrast.
seed_details.rebuttal: That program assumes global exclusion and does not characterize the selected-trust feasible relation or an outcome-ordered transport support function; nevertheless the absence of a plausible linear-size closed form lowers feasibility.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The contribution would have to be the non-LP transport representation, not another generic linear program.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Section 6 was read. Its single confidence region already covers any fixed finite collection of linear causal functionals simultaneously.
seed_details.question: Allow the analyst to select a trusted subset from the observed table and report valid post-selection bounds.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project one simultaneous cell-probability region through every candidate trusted-set envelope before selection.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair is already occupied in substance by simultaneous multinomial-region projection.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al.'s simultaneous confidence region because selection among finitely many projections cannot invalidate joint coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; absent a new selection target or optimality statement, this is a corollary rather than a research kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected as an inference add-on without an independent theorem shape.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The Introduction, response-type linear-program construction, eight-piece ATE formulas, multivalued-treatment discussion, and final applications were read from the JASA article.
seed_details.question: Use mixed-trust pairwise intervals to learn a minimax-regret categorical treatment policy under unmeasured confounding.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert all pairwise sharp supports into a coherent conditional welfare uncertainty set and optimize policy regret over it.
seed_details.destination_search: A search for categorical partial-identification policy learning found Hruza et al. (2026), who already give categorical minimax loss, differentiable surrogates, and oracle rates using causal bounds as inputs.
seed_details.red_team: Subsumed by Hruza et al.'s categorical partial-identification learning framework once the bounds are supplied.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for this formulation; a distinct policy kernel would need cross-pair coherence or a sharper regret frontier not presently supported.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected because the policy layer would merely consume the identification theorem.
